text: Bakanae, also called foolish seedling disease (ជំងឺខ្ពស់ដើម), is a fungal disease caused by Fusarium moniliforme. Infected plants grow noticeably taller than normal rice, with thin, pale yellow-green leaves. It can show up as early as the nursery stage and continue to be visible after transplanting. Affected plants tiller poorly compared to healthy plants nearby, despite being taller than normal. Infected plants often fail to produce a full, well-filled panicle, and some produce only empty (unfilled) grain. The fungus spreads plant-to-plant through wind and water contact; using seed harvested from infected plants is a major way the disease carries over to the next season. High nitrogen fertilization and warm temperatures (around 30–35°C) favor disease development. Management: (1) avoid saving seed from fields that had visible bakanae symptoms; (2) plant resistant varieties where available; (3) remove and destroy visibly infected plants from the field promptly; (4) disinfect seed before planting to kill any fungus carried on the seed coat.
